title: Fatality report finds police shooting of Calgary man justified
article: A fatality report says a Calgary police officer who shot a man after he had taken his neighbour hostage, acted in self-defence.
In May 2009, 49-year-old Melvin Donald Vanhouwe was shot several times at a home in the community of Southwood, by an officer with the tactical unit.
The incident began when Vanhouwe showed up uninvited at his neighbour's barbecue. At one point in the evening, several people at the party decided they wanted to go to the casino.
Vanhouwe, who had been drinking, went home to change and became enraged when he returned to his neighbor's house to find the party-goers had left for the casino without him.
He then got a sawed-off shotgun and held his neighbour, a 19-year-old man, at gunpoint.
When police arrived, Vanhouwe ignored requests to put down the weapon and eventually pointed it at officers.
That's when an officer opened fire, shooting Vanhouwe several times. He died in hospital.
Police later recovered a number of weapons and explosive devices from Vanhouwe's home.
The fatality report concludes police had no other option because their safety was at risk.
